svg.title: Crowd coding: the path of a message through a shared room
svg.desc: A participant message passes the Google Chat webhook's access gate, the pause check and the bridge checks (reserved commands, per-sender rate limit, bound-thread routing), then the message queue, before one shared-session turn. App commands, the pause queue, reserved commands, bound task sessions and the governance turn limits branch off the main path.

g.text: Hover a box for what it does; its connections light up. Click it to open the recipe section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: PIPELINE · A MESSAGE IN A SHARED ROOM
Crowd coding: the path of a message through a shared room
Pause, reserved commands and the rate limit are decided before a message can reach a session or a task.

g.text: message
allowed
not paused
not consumed
one turn
app command
paused
reserved
bound thread
every turn
reply
participants and facilitators
a trusted group in one Google Chat Space
facilitators are the senders in governance.admin_senders
participants and facilitators · participants write in ordinary language; facilitators are the senders listed in governance.admin_senders
An empty admin_senders list makes every sender an administrator, so list your facilitators.
Google Chat webhook
access gate: group_access, group_allowlist, require_mention
answers a registered app command here, then stops
a message also sent through Space Events counts once
Google Chat webhook · the webhook applies the access gate before anything else: group_access and the group allowlist, then require_mention
Without Space Events only @mentions arrive; a message that arrives both ways is processed once.
pause check
session key from group_scope: shared, thread-binding lookup
paused and not a reserved command: held in the pause queue
pause check · derives the session key (group_scope: shared gives one session per Space), looks up a task thread binding, then checks pause
A held message keeps its route, so /resume replays it into the right session.
bridge checks, in this order
reserved command: run or refused, then consumed
per-sender rate limit, admins exempt
bound thread: routed to that task's session
a message consumed by a check stops here
bridge checks, in this order · reserved commands, then the per-sender rate limit, then bound-thread routing; a consumed message stops
The rate limit comes before bound-thread routing, so a limited sender cannot bypass it inside a bound thread.
message queue
messages from one sender within 1 s join one prompt
one turn per session at a time; queue_strategy: fair
message queue · debounces for 1 s (channels.debounce_window_ms), runs one turn per session at a time, and with fair rotates senders
Bound-thread messages and a resumed pause queue enter here too, under the session key they were routed to.
group session turn
model and effort: governance.crowd_coding
tools: task_*, review_list, workflow_*, attach_media
one conversation shared by every participant
group session turn · the message is saved and one primary-lane turn runs; the agent calls registered tools, no chat grammar is parsed
Model and effort come from the group allowlist row and session or channel settings, then governance.crowd_coding, then the provider default.
Google Chat app commands
/new <description>, /reset, /status, /stop, /pause, /resume
/stop, /pause, /resume need an admin sender
answered before the bridge: no rate limit applies
Google Chat app commands · /new starts a task, /reset a fresh session, /status reports; /stop, /pause, /resume need an admin sender
Handled in the webhook after the access gate, so neither the pause queue nor the per-sender rate limit applies to them.
pause queue
/pause: new messages wait in memory; a restart empties it
/resume → 5
pause queue · while paused, reserved commands still run and every other message is queued (200 in all, plus max_pause_queued per sender)
/resume replays the queue grouped by session as one "While paused, N participants sent messages" prompt into the message queue.
reserved commands
/stop /pause /resume /bind /unbind, matched exactly
/stop cancels turns and tasks; non-admins refused, audited
reserved commands · consumed whether run or refused; a non-admin sender is refused and one audit entry is written when admin_senders is set
/stop cancels active turns and every running or queued task and broadcasts an emergency_stop event.
bound task session
a thread bound to a live task goes to that task's session
bound task session · with features.thread_binding.enabled, a message in a thread bound to a live task is queued on that task's session
Bindings come from /bind, task_bind and the first task notification; they end when the task is terminal or after idle_timeout_minutes (default 60).
turn limits (governance)
rate_limits.global: turn starts per window, all senders
budget.daily_tokens: action block or warn
loop_detection: action abort or warn
turn limits (governance) · limits that apply to every turn, whoever sent the message; admin senders are not exempt from any of the three
budget.daily_tokens refuses new turns once spent (action: block); an in-flight turn may finish past the threshold.
reply in the room
same Space, same thread when the message had one
redacted, formatted and split into chunks
reply in the room · the reply returns to the Space, in the message's thread when it has one
Outbound text passes the redactor, then Google Chat formatting and chunking.
